summary: Evidence Integration convergence through Sep. 11 16:22 ET. SIDR same-event chronology correction is separately specified because current v2 chronology is append-only.

events.summary: The IAEA Board of Governors reported Iran's safeguards non-compliance to the UN Security Council and General Assembly. AP reported a 23-3 vote with eight abstentions and one member not voting. This referral is not itself Security Council action or a new UN sanction.

Iranian Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei publicly argued that politicized IAEA action could push states toward leaving the NPT. This records an Iranian policy warning, not an Iranian NPT withdrawal.

Houthi forces seized Mocha and advanced onto the Hanish islands according to Yemeni and regional reporting. Reuters sources also alleged Iranian arms, advice and guidance; direct IRGC operational command remains source-reported and is not promoted to established fact.

Houthi forces captured Dhubab and Perim/Mayun Island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Yemeni government sources reported by Reuters and independent AP reporting. The gains materially improve Houthi geographic position around the chokepoint but do not establish control of all vessel transit.

OFAC designated Iran-linked and terrorist-support networks including Kata'ib Hizballah and Lebanese Hizballah-linked targets and changed Iran-related specific-license treatment to a presumption of denial, with stated narrow exceptions. The licensing policy change was effective immediately.

Iran temporarily suspended its 10% freight charge on foreign vessels transporting oil, gas and liquid petroleum products to or from Iran pending approval and publication of a definitive taxable-products list, according to Fars reporting carried by Reuters.

Kpler counted seven observable vessel transits through Hormuz on September 10, down from 11 the previous day and below a 10-day average of 15. Five were inbound and two outbound. AIS-off/dark traffic is excluded.

Baltic Exchange data reported by Reuters put Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC freight around Worldscale 450, roughly $11.50 per barrel, a record for that route series; West Africa-to-Asia VLCC rates also reached record levels.

South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held a call on Hormuz and regional security. Seoul told Iran that no decision had been made on a possible South Korean military deployment.

President Masoud Pezeshkian publicly said Iranian imports and exports had fallen by roughly 25% to 35% and rejected claims that sanctions had no effect. The percentage is retained as the president's own economic estimate, not an independently audited trade statistic.

Later reporting established a long operational tail from the March Ras Laffan strikes: two of QatarEnergy's 14 LNG trains and a GTL facility were damaged; QatarEnergy's CEO had said 12.8 mtpa of LNG capacity would be sidelined for three to five years, and production remained halted while force-majeure notices continued.

The IEA assessed Saudi August crude supply at about 6 million barrels per day, down 2.3 million bpd month-on-month and the lowest level in more than three decades, after attacks disrupted facilities and shipping.

Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said the East-West oil pipeline was temporarily shut after multiple attacks in the Riyadh and Medina regions. The shutdown/effect is established at authority-report level; the responsible attacker was not established in the ministry account.

record.disposition: CENTCOM primary video/caption states M/T Riesco sank in the Gulf of Oman on Sep. 8 after the U.S. strike.
U.S. official told Reuters one A-10 was severely damaged, including a missing wing.
U.S. official told Reuters roughly eight F-15s were lightly damaged and returned to service.

record.name: Muwaffaq al-Salti / Azraq Air Base
record.current_presence_status: U.S. aircraft and personnel presence established by Sep. 8 strike BDA reporting.
verified_physical_damage: Later U.S.-official reporting establishes severe damage to one A-10 and light damage to roughly eight F-15s on Sep. 8.
continued_operation_evidence: Roughly eight F-15s were reported lightly damaged and returned to service.
record.assessment: Aircraft damage is now established. Exact aircraft count/details remain source-bounded to an anonymous U.S. official; early Jordanian interception/fall reporting remains preserved rather than overwritten.

verified_physical_damage: Damage to Qatar LNG export infrastructure sufficient to reduce export capacity materially.
Later reporting identifies two of 14 LNG trains and a gas-to-liquids facility as damaged.
verified_functional_effect: QatarEnergy CEO said 12.8 million tonnes per year of LNG capacity would be sidelined for three to five years.
Reuters reported QatarEnergy had halted production in March and continued renewing force-majeure notices.
repair_evidence: Multi-year U.S. LNG replacement-contract discussions through 2031 were reported by industry/trading sources.
record.assessment: Physical damage affected a subset of the system, while production halt and force majeure establish a broader operational effect. A Qatar-linked cargo transit does not by itself establish production restart.

record.observed_traffic: Kpler counted seven observable vessel transits on Sep. 10, down from 11 the previous day and below the same-provider 10-day average of 15; five entered and two exited.
record.ais_scope: Kpler observable vessel traffic only. AIS-off/dark traffic is excluded. Broader pre-war large-commercial-vessel figures are contextual and are not a like-for-like denominator.
record.note: Use the same-provider 11/day prior-day and 15/day 10-day average for direct comparison. Do not equate observable AIS traffic with all physical transit.
